Or: October 25, 1929, a letter was received, 
addressed to the Conmissioner of Police, from a Mr. 
C.K.P. Ching. ‘This gentleman claimed to have know- 
ledge resarding, the whereabouts of a certain person 
for whose arrest a reward was offered some years 
previously. 


As A/ A.C. (Crime) I was instructed to inter- 
view the writer, which I did in my office on October 
28. 


Mr. Ching intimated to me that he could supply 
information which would lead to the arrest of the sut- 
ject of Wanted Notice No. 727, issued August 17, 1927; 
but would not do so until he was assured a reward 
would be forthcoming, 


I instructed Senior Detective ifce Central to 
ascertain whether the rewards as shown on the notice 
referred to still heid good. He reported that the 
firm of Mohamad Dund & Co., who formerly offered *700. 
reward, had given up their Shanghai business and re- 
turned to India. Messrs. Musso, Fischer & Wilhelm, 
however, on behalf of tho Banks interested, were pre- 
pared to confirm their original offer of £1000. reward 
and addressed a letter to this effect to ths Commissioner 
of Police on October Zl. 

I informed Mr. Ching accordingly eat a subsequent 
interview, and he then gave information that the wanted 
man was in Hankow. 


I leter interviewed Dr. Wilhelm and a represen- 
tative of the Banks, informed them that the man in 
question was living some distance away and it would 
cost between three and four hundred dollars to bring 
him to Shanghai. These expensos, I was informed, would 
have to be deducted from the #1000. reward, as no fur- 
ther sum for this purpose was available. 


I notified Mr. Ching to this effect, he agreed 
to this arrangement and then supplied full particulars 
of the wanted men's exact whereabouts in Hankow. 


Sone little difficulty was then experienced in 
obtaining the services of an identifier. One was even- 
tually secured and he left for Hankow with C.D.C.s 54 
and 60 on November 25. They succeeded in locating and 
arresting the man and returned to Shanghai on December 7. 


The man appeared before the Provisional Court on 
December 9, and after a preliminary hearing was remanded 
in custody until December 30. Full particulars of the 
case were forwarded to Police Advocate. Dr. Wilhelm 
appeared on behalf of the Banks who are complainants 
in the case.

"A" Division,
December 16, 1929.

Summary of facts relating to the arrest of Dzeu Tsung
Nan (鄭正南) referred to in attached file.

On October 25, 1929, a letter was received,
addressed to the Commissioner of Police, from a Mr.
C.K.P. Ching. This gentleman claimed to have know-
ledge regarding the whereabouts of a certain person
for whose arrest a reward was offered some years
previously.

As A/ A.C. (Crime) I was instructed to inter-
view the writer, which I did in my office on October
28.

Mr. Ching intimated to me that he could supply
information which would lead to the arrest of the sub-
ject of Wanted Notice No. 727, issued August 17, 1927;
but would not do so until he was assured a reward
would be forthcoming.

I instructed Senior Detective i/c Central to
ascertain whether the rewards as shown on the notice
referred to still held good. He reported that the
firm of Mohamad Dund & Co., who formerly offered $700.
reward, had given up their Shanghai business and re-
turned to India. Messrs. Musso, Fischer & Wilhelm,
however, on behalf of the Banks interested, were pre-
pared to confirm their original offer of $1000. reward
and addressed a letter to this effect to the Commissioner
of Police on October 31.

I informed Mr. Ching accordingly at a subsequent
interview, and he then gave information that the wanted
man was in Hankow.

I later interviewed Dr. Wilhelm and a represen-
tative of the Banks, informed them that the man in
question was living some distance away and it would
cost between three and four hundred dollars to bring
him to Shanghai. These expenses, I was informed, would
have to be deducted from the $1000. reward, as no fur-
ther sum for this purpose was available.

I notified Mr. Ching to this effect, he agreed
to this arrangement and then supplied full particulars
of the wanted man's exact whereabouts in Hankow.

Some little difficulty was then experienced in
obtaining the services of an identifier. One was even-
tually secured and he left for Hankow with C.D.C.s 54
and 60 on November 25. They succeeded in locating and
arresting the man and returned to Shanghai on December 7.

The man appeared before the Provisional Court on
December 9, and after a preliminary hearing was remanded
in custody until December 30. Full particulars of the
case were forwarded to Police Advocate. Dr. Wilhelm
appeared on behalf of the Banks who are complainants
in the case.

D. D. O. (A)

“A”分区，
1929年12月16日。

关于附件卷宗中提及的郑正南（Dzeu Tsung Nan）被捕一案的事实摘要。

1929年10月25日，警务处总监收到一封来自C.K.P. Ching先生的信件。该先生声称知晓数年前曾悬赏缉拿的某人的下落。

作为代理助理总监（刑事），我奉命约谈写信人，并于10月28日在我的办公室进行了约谈。

Ching先生向我暗示，他能提供线索以逮捕1927年8月17日发布的第727号通缉令所指的对象；但在确保能获得赏金之前，他不愿提供线索。

我指示中央巡捕房负责高级侦探查明上述通缉令所列赏金是否仍然有效。他报告称，原先提供700美元赏金的Mohamad Dund & Co.公司已放弃其在上海的业务并返回印度。然而，Musso, Fischer & Wilhelm公司代表相关银行，准备确认其原先提供的1000美元赏金，并于10月31日致信警务处总监说明此事。

我在随后的约谈中将此情况告知了Ching先生，他随即提供了该通缉犯在汉口的信息。

此后我会见了Wilhelm博士及银行代表，告知他们该人居住地较远，将其押解至上海需花费三百至四百美元。我获悉，这笔费用须从1000美元赏金中扣除，因为无额外款项可用于此目的。

我将此情况通知了Ching先生，他同意了这一安排，随后提供了该通缉犯在汉口的确切藏身之处的全部详情。

当时在寻找一名辨认人方面遇到了一些困难。最终找到了一名辨认人，他于11月25日随同中央侦探课第54号和第60号警员前往汉口。他们成功 locating 并逮捕了该人，于12月7日返回上海。

该人于12月9日出庭受审于临时法院，经初步聆讯后还押候审至12月30日。案件的全部详情已移送警务检察官。Wilhelm博士代表本案原告银行出庭。

Sir,
I, C.D.C. 60 Lui Kyung Ching (刘俊卿) attached to Central Police Station, beg to state that at 10.30 p.m. on the 25th November 1929, accompanied by C.D.C. 54, I proceeded to Hankow from S'hai on board S.S. Tih Woo. We arrived in Hankow at 9.30 a.m. on the 28th November 1929 and rented a room in the "Tong Soong Hotel" At 11a.m. on the same day we disguised as coolies and went to wait for the accused Dzau Tsaung Hen at the door of the Ewo Godown on Bund, but that godown is in a large building, so we could not ascertain in which place Dzau was working for. We waited until 1.30 p.m., but we could not locate him. We then returned to the Hotel and took some food, whilst we then planned how to locate Dzau. I then wrote a Chinese letter bearing the accused's name on the envelope and stating that this letter must be delivered personally. Dear Sir,

Upon examination of a sister-in-law, and a maid
servant of Siw Chong Nang, we have received their answers
as follows:-

I. Sister-in-law ( 邵徐氏 Elder brother's wife ) was
born in Canton and is forty years of age.

Her husband is by the name of 吕龄 , and at present
engaging in business at Hupeh district ( 湖北 - )

Recently Chong Nang didn't care about his family,
so that his family have to get support from 吕龄 . She
does not know about Chong Nang's recent doings and where-
abouts.

II. The maid servant was born in Canton and is 15 years
of age and is a slave girl of Siw Chong Nang's mother.
Siw Chong Nang has never been with his mother since just
before the recent disturbances in Shanghai, but the means
of the mother's livelihood had been given by Chong Nang
through another person.

Siw Chong Nang's wife is now in Canton, besides
he keeps a concubine in Shanghai, once in the ground floor
at No.5 of 1st row, 青映路德安里 , and now in the new
building at 武昌路章泰里 , but the number of address
in unknown.

His mother's monthly expenses was given by this
concubine, but this has been discontinued since the distur-
bances occured in Shanghai.

This servant knows nothing about 邵鳳岐 (Chong
Nang's elder brother)

Judging from these examinations, we understand
that their answers seemed to be correct and true and they
haven't any connections with this case, hence we cannot
keep them in custody.

Regarding Chong Nang's concubine, who is at present
living in 武昌路 within the Foreign Settlement, you can
ask the Municipal Police to examine her.

Yours faithfully,

already
investigated by attached
by Detective Station
Central J.Hoffman
pages.zh:
亲爱的先生：

经讯问 Siw Chong Nang（邵昌南）的嫂子和一名女仆，我们得到如下答复：—

I. 嫂子（邵徐氏，兄长的妻子）出生于广州，现年四十岁。

其丈夫名为吕龄，目前在湖北地区经商。

最近昌南不顾家庭，以致其家人不得不依靠吕龄供养。她不知道昌南最近的行踪和下落。

II. 女仆出生于广州，现年15岁，是 Siw Chong Nang 母亲的婢女。自上海近期发生骚乱前不久起，Siw Chong Nang 就未与其母亲在一起，但其母亲的生活费一直由昌南通过他人提供。

Siw Chong Nang 的妻子目前在广州，此外他在上海纳有一妾，起初住在青映路德安里第一排5号的一楼，现在住在武昌路章泰里的新楼房内，但具体门牌号码不详。

其母亲的月度开销由这名妾室提供，但自上海发生骚乱以来已停止。

这名女仆对邵凤岐（昌南的兄长）一无所知。

根据这些讯问，我们认为她们的供述似乎是正确和真实的，且她们与本案没有任何牵连，因此我们不能拘留她们。

关于昌南的妾室，她目前居住在公共租界内的武昌路，您可以要求工部局警务处对其进行讯问。

您忠实的，

August 9th, 1927.

REPORT ON Chinese Compradore obtaining money by Fraud.

Made by D. I. Hunter, Forwarded by Conway, Insp.

Sir,

I beg to report that on August 6th, 1927, Dr. Wilhelm came to this Station and reported that on July 25th, 1927, the Compradore of Mohamad Daud & Co., No. 32 North Soochow Road, named Siw Chang Nan (许昌南) had obtained from four different banks to total sum Taels 59,215.94 also taking from Mohamad Daud & Co. $6,000.00 and absconded on or about 4th or 5th August 1927. The result of Police enquiries are briefly as follows:-

In January 1927, Mr. Daud the Manager of Mohamad Daud & Co. left for India, and prior to leaving Shanghai arranged with the different Foreign Banks that the Compradore Siw Chang Nan (许昌南) had power of attorney for the Company and allowed to sign all official documents and cheques, at the same time Mr. Daud left a young man named Jalal-Ur-Rahman to act as Foreign representative for the Co. which deals extensively in Silks and Tea, but gave him no control over the funds of the Company leaving that entirely in the hands of Siw Chang Nan the Compradore.

On July 23rd, 1927, Siw Chang Nan shipped on the S. S. Rangoon Maru 1265 cases of tea consigned to Mohamad Daud & Co. Head Offices Peshawar City, which were supposed to contain a first class China Tea, but it later transpired that all the cases were filled with tea dust and sweepings. Two days after the tea was shipped ( July 25th, 1927 ) Siw Chang Nan presented the false invoices to the different Banks and obtained the money which was later passed through different Foreign and Chinese Banks.

The following are the Banks etc. involved:-
P & O Banking Corporation Ltd. $10,057.80

先生，

卑职谨此报告，1927 年 8 月 6 日，Wilhelm 博士来到本分局报案称，1927 年 7 月 25 日，苏州北路 32 号 Mohamad Daud & Co. 商号的买办，名为 Siw Chang Nan（许昌南），从四家不同银行骗取总计规元银 59,215.94 两，并从 Mohamad Daud & Co. 商号拿走 6,000.00 美元，于 1927 年 8 月 4 日或 5 日左右潜逃。警方调查结果简述如下：—

1927 年 1 月，Mohamad Daud & Co. 商号经理 Daud 先生前往印度，在离开上海前，他与各家外国银行安排，授权该商号买办 Siw Chang Nan（许昌南）拥有公司代理权，允许签署所有官方文件和支票；同时，Daud 先生留下一名名为 Jalal-Ur-Rahman 的青年担任该公司的外籍代表，该公司主要从事丝绸和茶叶贸易，但未赋予其对公司资金的管控权，将资金完全交由买办 Siw Chang Nan 掌管。

1927 年 7 月 23 日，Siw Chang Nan 将 1265 箱茶叶装上“Rangoon Maru”号轮船，收货人为 Mohamad Daud & Co. 位于白沙瓦市的总部，这些货物据称装有上等中国茶叶，但后来查明所有箱子装的都是茶末和清扫物。茶叶装运两天后（1927 年 7 月 25 日），Siw Chang Nan 向各家银行出示虚假发票，骗得款项，随后通过多家外国和中国银行转账。
